content.user_title: Build Azure Event Hubs Clients in Rust
content.value_statement: Rust developers need reliable patterns for Azure Event Hubs producers and consumers. This skill provides focused setup, sending, receiving, batching, and checkpointing guidance.
actual_capabilities: Configures Azure Event Hubs Rust dependencies and endpoint variables.
Creates authenticated producer and consumer clients with DeveloperToolsCredential.
Sends individual events and batches through ProducerClient.
Receives events from a selected partition and inspects their bodies.
Retrieves hub and partition properties and identifies optional checkpoint storage.
limitations: Covers only basic SDK flows and omits full application structure.
Uses DeveloperToolsCredential and does not compare production identity options.
Does not provide retry, error classification, telemetry, or deployment configuration.
Requires environment-specific testing against an accessible Azure Event Hubs namespace.

use_cases.title: Prototype an event producer
use_cases.description: Create a Rust client that authenticates, builds a batch, and sends events to an existing Event Hub.

use_cases.title: Inspect partition events
use_cases.description: Open a partition receiver, collect a bounded event set, and inspect event bodies during integration work.

use_cases.title: Plan distributed consumption
use_cases.description: Review consumer groups, parallel partition processing, and optional Blob checkpoint storage before designing a distributed consumer.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic producer
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the dependencies, endpoint variables, and Rust steps needed to send one event to my Azure Event Hub.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single-event producer

prompt_templates.title: Send events in batches
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Rust producer flow that creates batches, checks capacity, and sends my event payloads efficiently.

prompt_templates.title: Build a partition consumer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Rust consumer approach for partition {partition_id}, receiving at most {event_count} events and reporting Event Hub properties.

prompt_templates.title: Design distributed processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose an Azure Event Hubs Rust consumer design using consumer groups, parallel partition processing, and Blob checkpoint storage. Identify missing production concerns.

output_examples.input: Create a Rust producer that sends two messages as one batch.
output: Dependency and credential setup for the Azure Event Hubs producer.
A batching flow that adds both payloads and checks available capacity.
A send step with validation notes for the target namespace and hub.

output_examples.input: Help me inspect up to 100 events from partition zero.
output: A consumer setup using the configured namespace and Event Hub name.
A bounded receive flow for partition zero.
Guidance for inspecting event bodies and handling environment-specific failures.

output_examples.input: Review my plan for several consumer instances.
output: Recommendations for consumer groups and parallel partition ownership.
A checkpoint storage option for coordinated progress tracking.
A list of production gaps, including retries, telemetry, and deployment validation.

best_practices: Reuse producer and consumer clients across operations.
Batch events when practical and verify capacity before adding each event.
Use consumer groups and checkpointing for coordinated distributed consumers.
anti_patterns: Do not create a new client for every event.
Do not assume every event fits in the current batch.
Do not deploy distributed consumers without a checkpointing and partition ownership strategy.

faq.question: Which Rust crates does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers azure_messaging_eventhubs, azure_identity, and the optional Azure Blob checkpoint store crate.

faq.question: Can it create both producers and consumers?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides basic patterns for sending events, batching payloads, receiving partition events, and reading service properties.

faq.question: Does it configure Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. You need an existing namespace, Event Hub, permissions, and valid local or workload credentials.

faq.question: Does it provide production authentication guidance?
faq.answer: Only partially. The examples use DeveloperToolsCredential and do not compare managed identity or other production credential options.

faq.question: Does it handle retries and monitoring?
faq.answer: No. Add application-specific retry policies, error handling, metrics, tracing, and operational alerts.

faq.question: When should I use checkpoint storage?
faq.answer: Use checkpoint storage when distributed consumers must coordinate partition ownership and resume processing from recorded progress.
